The Preserved Qur'an

Imami scholars from al-Saduq to al-Sistani hold that the Qur'an between the two covers is the Qur'an God sent down. Imami books carry reports of loss, and Sunni books carry reports of scribal error. Al-Tusi classed the Imami reports as solitary, and Sunni scholars graded the Sunni reports sound, interpreted them or rejected them. Scholars of both schools disputed what the reports show.

Premise 1. Ibn Hazm charged the Imamiyya with holding that the Qur'an was changed, with words added and many removed. He exempted one Imami and two companions. Al-Safadi quotes the charge in his entry on al-Sharif al-Murtada. His quotation names the exempted man Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa, which is al-Murtada's name.
Premise 2. The Qur'an uses tahrif for moving words from their places and meanings. Al-Khoei names the loss of revealed text as the sense of tahrif that Muslims dispute.

Premise 3. Al-Kafi carries reports of a larger revelation and of verses Jibril brought "in this form" with a name added. It also carries a report of a scribal error in Qur'an 5:95. Sunni books carry reports in which Ibn Abbas calls words of the codex a scribe's error.

Premise 4. The Imams ﵈ told their followers to judge reports by the Qur'an. They also told them to recite as the people recite until al-Qa'im rises. Al-Tusi classes the reports of loss as solitary reports, which yield neither certain knowledge nor grounds for action.

Premise 5. Al-Saduq, al-Murtada, al-Khoei, al-Tabataba'i, al-Khomeini and al-Sistani hold that the Qur'an in Muslim hands is the Qur'an God sent down. Al-Tabrisi calls that the sound view of the school, and al-Tusi calls it the view more fitting for the sound position of his school. Al-Majlisi, and al-Fayd al-Kashani in al-Safi, read some reports as evidence of loss.

Conclusion. Imami scholars including al-Saduq, al-Murtada, al-Khoei, al-Tabataba'i, al-Khomeini and al-Sistani affirm the received Qur'an, and some Imami scholars accepted reports of omission. Sunni books carry reports of scribal error, which Sunni scholars accepted, interpreted or rejected. Al-Tusi classed the Imami reports of loss as solitary, and scholars of both schools disputed what the reports show. Ibn Hazm's charge presents that dispute as the doctrine of the Imamiyya.

The Charge Ibn Hazm Recorded
Source: Ibn Hazm, al-Fisal fi al-Milal wa al-Ahwa' wa al-Nihal, vol.4, p.182; al-Safadi, al-Wafi bil-Wafayat, vol.21, pp.2-3
Speaker: Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi (d.456 AH); Salah al-Din al-Safadi (d.764 AH)
Claim: all Imamiyya hold the Qur'an was altered, except one named Imami and his two companions

Ibn Hazm, an Andalusian scholar, surveys religions and sects in al-Fisal. He attributes the view of an altered Qur'an to all the Imamiyya, the Imami Shia, early and late. He exempts one Imami with Mu'tazili leanings. The printed al-Fisal names him Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Musa and traces his descent to Musa ibn Ja'far. Ibn Hazm reports that this man rejected the view and called its holders unbelievers. He reports the same of two companions, Abu Ya'la Milad al-Tusi and Abu al-Qasim al-Razi.

Al-Safadi, a biographer of the eighth century AH, quotes this passage in his entry on al-Sharif al-Murtada. The entry opens with al-Murtada's lineage, Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa, traced to Musa ibn Ja'far. In the quotation, Ibn Hazm exempts a man of that same name, so al-Safadi treats the exempted man as al-Murtada. The printed al-Fisal gives the lineage in a different form. It has al-Hasan where al-Safadi has al-Husayn, at the start and near the end of the chain. It also lacks one Musa between Muhammad and Ibrahim. The identification of the exempted man with al-Murtada therefore rests on al-Safadi's quotation of Ibn Hazm.
What Tahrif Means
Source: al-Jawhari, al-Sihah, vol.4, p.31; Ibn Manzur, Lisan al-Arab, vol.9, p.43
Speaker: two classical lexicographers
Claim: tahrif of speech is changing it, and the Qur'an uses the verb for changing meanings

Al-Jawhari defines the tahrif of speech as changing it from its places. Ibn Manzur says the Jews changed the meanings of the Torah by look-alikes. He quotes the Qur'an's words "they distort words from their places", which occur in Qur'an 4:46 and 5:13.
Verse: Qur'an 4:46
Claim: some of the Jews distort words from their places

The Qur'an uses the verb four times, in Qur'an 2:75, 4:46, 5:13 and 5:41. Each verse describes people who alter the sense or the place of words in an earlier scripture. None of the four verses applies the verb to the Qur'an.
Source: al-Khoei, al-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Qur'an, pp.197 and 200
Speaker: Sayyid Abu al-Qasim al-Khoei (d.1413 AH)
Claim: tahrif has several senses, and loss of text is the one in dispute among Muslims

Al-Khoei sorts the senses of tahrif by whether Muslims agree they occurred. His first sense is moving a thing from its place, and he applies it to interpreting a verse against its meaning. He says all Muslims agree that this kind of tahrif occurred. His fifth sense is addition of material that is not revealed speech, which he calls false by consensus. His sixth sense is omission, and he names it as the sense in dispute. The passages quoted here leave out his second to fourth senses. A report that uses the word tahrif may therefore mean a false interpretation. To support a charge of loss, a report has to speak of lost text.

Two positions below conflict with al-Khoei's claim of consensus on addition. Al-Mufid allows that a word or a letter could be added to the Qur'an. Al-Mazandarani reads the report on Qur'an 5:95 as a copyist's added letter.
The Guarantee of Qur'an 15:9
Verse: Qur'an 15:9
Claim: God sent down the Reminder and guards it
Source: al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan fi Tafsir al-Qur'an, vol.12, p.107
Speaker: Allama Muhammad Husayn al-Tabataba'i (d.1402 AH)
Claim: the Qur'an in hand carries every attribute God gave it, so it is the Qur'an sent down

Al-Tabataba'i reasons from the Qur'an's attributes to its text. God described the Qur'an as inimitable, free of discrepancy, guiding and luminous. If addition, omission or a change of wording or order had altered those attributes, their traces would show the change. The Qur'an in hand carries those traces in full, so he concludes it is the Qur'an sent down. A dropped repeated verse, or a difference in a dot or a vowel, would leave the attributes intact. He says any loss, if one supposes it, would have to be of that kind.
Reports in al-Kafi
Source: al-Kulayni, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.634, no.28, the last report of Kitab Fadl al-Qur'an; al-Kafi is cited throughout by the printed pages of the Dar al-Kutub al-Islamiyya edition
Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Hisham ibn Salim
Dating: compiled by al-Kulayni (d.329 AH)
Claim: the Qur'an Jibril brought to Muhammad ﷺ was seventeen thousand verses
The report's seventeen thousand verses exceed the verse count of the Qur'an in hand.
Al-Saduq gives the same figure and assigns the excess to revelation that is not Qur'an.
Source: al-Majlisi, Mir'at al-Uqul, quoted with a reply in al-Milani, al-Tahqiq fi Nafy al-Tahrif, pp.86-88
Speaker: al-Allama al-Majlisi (d.1110 AH), answered by Sayyid Ali al-Milani
Claim: this report and many sound reports state loss, and their meaning is mutawatir

Al-Milani quotes al-Majlisi's comment on a report that al-Majlisi graded muwaththaq, reliable through trustworthy narrators who include non-Imamis. Al-Majlisi then calls the reports of loss mutawatir in meaning. Mutawatir means reported by so many routes that the shared meaning is certain. He judges them at least equal to the reports on the imamate.

Al-Milani answers that al-Majlisi's Bihar al-Anwar calls such reports solitary. He cites al-Murtada, al-Tusi, al-Fayd and al-Saduq against the claim of soundness. He adds that al-Majlisi graded most of the al-Kafi reports of loss weak or mursal. A mursal report has a gap in its chain. Al-Milani asks whether that equality refers to number, strength of meaning or soundness of chains.
Source: al-Kafi, vol.2, p.633, no.23
Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Salim ibn Salama
Claim: a man is told to stop a non-standard reading and to recite as the people recite until al-Qa'im rises

Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ stops the man's reading and tells him to recite as the people recite. The instruction holds until al-Qa'im, the Riser from the Prophet's ﷺ house, rises. The Imam ﵇ says al-Qa'im will bring out the codex Ali ﵇ wrote. He recounts that Ali ﵇ offered that codex as the Book sent down to Muhammad ﷺ. The people answered that their own codex held the whole Qur'an. The report sets Ali's ﵇ codex apart from the circulating copy, and it does not say how the two differed.
Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, p.228, no.1
Speaker: Imam al-Baqir ﵇, through Jabir
Claim: whoever claims to have gathered the whole Qur'an as it was revealed is a liar, except Ali ﵇ and the Imams after him

The chapter heading says that only the Imams gathered the whole Qur'an and that "they know all of its knowledge". Jabir's report says Ali ﵇ and the Imams after him gathered and memorized it "as God Most High sent it down". The report gives no account of what the people's copy lacked.
Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, p.417, no.26, in the chapter of points and fragments from the tanzil on wilaya, vol.1, pp.412-436
Speaker: Jabir, by the chain of the preceding report in that chapter
Claim: Jibril brought Qur'an 2:23 with words about Ali ﵇

Reports of this form add a name to a verse and say Jibril brought the verse "in this form". Al-Kulayni gathered them in a chapter on wilaya, the authority of the Imams. Al-Tabataba'i reads such wording as the explanation that accompanied the revelation, as quoted below.
Source: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.226; al-Muhammadi, Salamat al-Qur'an min al-Tahrif, p.120; al-Khoei, Mu'jam Rijal al-Hadith, vol.3, p.71
Speaker: al-Khoei; Fath Allah al-Muhammadi; al-Najashi, quoted by al-Khoei
Claim: many such reports have weak chains, a large share come from al-Sayyari, and some come by reliable routes

Al-Khoei says many reports of tahrif have weak chains. He traces a number of them to the book of Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari and others to Ali ibn Ahmad al-Kufi. Al-Najashi calls al-Sayyari weak in hadith and corrupt in doctrine, with many mursal reports. Al-Muhammadi counts 350 of the 1,602 reports gathered by the hadith scholar al-Nuri as coming from al-Sayyari's Book of Recitations. Al-Khoei grants that the number of reports makes it certain that some came from the Imams ﵈. He holds that none of them indicates tahrif in the disputed sense, the loss of text.
How the School Weighs a Solitary Report
Source: al-Tusi, al-Tibyan fi Tafsir al-Qur'an, vol.1, p.77
Speaker: Shaykh al-Ta'ifa al-Tusi (d.460 AH)
Claim: reports of loss are solitary, yield neither knowledge nor grounds for action, and are best set aside

Al-Tusi calls addition invalid by consensus. He calls the denial of loss the apparent position of Muslims and the view more fitting for the sound position of his school. He grants that narrators of his school and of the general body of Muslims transmit many reports of loss and of moved verses. He classes them as solitary reports, which yield neither certain knowledge nor grounds for action. He adds that even a sound report of this kind would not challenge the text between the covers.
Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, p.69, no.5; al-Hurr al-Amili, Wasa'il al-Shi'a, vol.27, p.118, no.33362
Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, quoting the Prophet ﷺ; and Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abd Allah
Claim: a report that contradicts the Book of God is rejected

The Mina sermon makes the Book the test for any report from the Prophet ﷺ. The Wasa'il report makes it the test between two differing hadiths. A report that the Book was altered contradicts that Book, so it fails the test. Al-Fayd al-Kashani applies this rule to the reports of alteration in al-Safi, quoted in the section on the scholars of the school.
Source: al-Kafi, vol.2, pp.630-631, nos.12, 13 and 15
Speaker: Imam al-Baqir ﵇ and Imam al-Sadiq ﵇
Claim: the Qur'an is one, sent down by One, and differences come from the narrators; recite as you were taught

Imam al-Baqir ﵇ says the Qur'an is one and the disagreement comes from the transmitters. Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ denies that the Qur'an came down in seven ahruf, modes of reading, and says it came down in one. Asked about the Qur'an's revelation, he answers, "Recite as you were taught."
Source: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, al-Musnad, vol.8, p.470, no.5057
Speaker: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ
Claim: two men taught different readings are told to recite as they were taught
Sunni books report the same words from the Prophet ﷺ.

In Ibn Mas'ud's report, two men each say the Prophet ﷺ taught them a sura. The Prophet ﷺ tells both to recite as they were taught. Each man keeps the reading he was taught. In Salim's report, the Imam ﵇ tells the man to recite as the people recite until al-Qa'im rises. The Prophet's ﷺ instruction leaves two readings in place, and the Imam's ﵇ instruction names one, the people's reading.
Source: al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, vol.12, p.108
Speaker: al-Tabataba'i
Claim: the Imams ﵈ argued from the Qur'an as it stands, and "it was revealed thus" means explanation

Al-Tabataba'i draws on three groups of reports. In the first, the Imams ﵈ cite verses on every subject in agreement with the Qur'an in hand. He takes this to show that "it was revealed thus" in many reports means the explanation that came with revelation. In the second, the Imams ﵈ call the people's Qur'an revealed by God, although it differs from Ali's ﵇ codex. The third is their instruction to recite as the people recite. He concludes that any difference from Ali's ﵇ codex lies only in the order of the suras or of some verses, whose reordering leaves the meaning unchanged.
Hammad's Report on Qur'an 5:95
Verse: Qur'an 5:95
Claim: two just men among you judge the equivalent of game killed in the state of ihram
Source: al-Kafi, vol.8, p.205, no.247, in al-Rawda
Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Hammad ibn Uthman
Claim: the dual dhawa 'adl, "two just men", is "among the things in which the kuttab erred", and the reading is dhu 'adl, "one just man"
Hammad recites the dual, and the Imam ﵇ answers with the singular and attributes the dual to the kuttab. The report concerns one letter, the alif that makes "one just man" into "two just men".
Al-Tabrisi records the singular as the reading of al-Baqir ﵇ and al-Sadiq ﵇. He lists it among the shawadhdh, readings reported outside the accepted readings.
In Zurara's report Imam al-Baqir ﵇ recites the dual. He names the two just men as the Messenger ﷺ and the Imam after him. Al-Tabrisi and Zurara therefore differ on what al-Baqir ﵇ recited.

On the common reading that al-Mazandarani reports, the kuttab erred by giving "two just men" a general application. Al-Mazandarani prefers a second reading, in which the kuttab were copyists and the revealed word was singular. Al-Tabataba'i also takes the kuttab to be the scribes of the codex. Al-Fayd suggests that the one just man is the infallible Imam. Al-Gulpaygani first reads the alif as a scribe's addition. He then judges the dual correct on the strength of Zurara's report. On the copyist reading, the report alleges a scribal error in the codex.
Parallel Reports in Sunni Books
Source: al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn, vol.2, p.396
Speaker: Ibn Abbas, through Mujahid
Dating: al-Hakim (d.405 AH) grades it sahih on the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim
Claim: the word tasta'nisu in Qur'an 24:27 is a scribe's error for tasta'dhinu
Source: Ibn Abi Hatim, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Azim, vol.8, pp.154-155, no.14560
Speaker: Ibn Abbas, through Ata'
Claim: "the likeness of His light" in Qur'an 24:35 is a scribe's error for "the light of the believer"

Abu Shahba quotes the exegete Abu Hayyan, who calls whoever reports the 24:27 statement from Ibn Abbas a heretic. Ibn Ashtah, quoted by al-Suyuti, explains the error as a poor choice among the seven ahruf. Ma'rifat, an Imami scholar, reviews ten such reports of early scribal error. He says they must be interpreted or rejected.
Al-Hakim graded the 24:27 report sahih by the standard of al-Bukhari and Muslim.
The Mushaf of Fatimah
Source: Abu Mansur al-Azhari, Tahdhib al-Lugha, vol.4, p.149; Murtada al-Askari, al-Mushaf fi al-Riwayat wa al-Athar, p.10
Speaker: al-Layth, quoted by al-Azhari; al-Askari
Claim: a mushaf is any bound collection of written pages
The Kafi reports speak of a Mushaf of Fatimah ﵍. The word mushaf means any bound collection of pages, as the two sources below define it.
Al-Layth defines the mushaf as written sheets gathered between two covers. Al-Askari concludes that the word names any bound book, Qur'an or not.
Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, pp.238-240, chapter on al-Sahifa, al-Jafr, al-Jami'a and the Mushaf of Fatimah, nos.1-3
Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Abu Basir, Hammad ibn Uthman and al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala'
Claim: the Mushaf of Fatimah ﵍ holds no letter of the Qur'an

In the first report Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ says the book is three times the size of the Qur'an. He swears it holds no letter of the Qur'an. In the second, an angel consoles Fatimah ﵍ after the Prophet's ﷺ death, and Ali ﵇ writes down what she hears. The Imam ﵇ says the book holds no law and holds knowledge of what will happen. In the third, he lists the Mushaf of Fatimah ﵍ among the contents of the White Jafr. He adds, "I do not claim that it contains a Qur'an."
Ali's Codex and His Teaching
Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, p.64, no.1, in the chapter on the difference of hadith, vol.1, pp.62-64
Speaker: Imam Ali ﵇, through Sulaym ibn Qays
Claim: Ali ﵇ wrote every verse in his own hand, and the Prophet ﷺ taught him its interpretation, abrogation and scope

Imam Ali ﵇ says the Prophet ﷺ dictated every revealed verse to him and he wrote it in his own hand. He says the Prophet ﷺ also taught him each verse's interpretation, its abrogating and abrogated verses, and its decisive and ambiguous verses. He adds that the Prophet ﷺ prayed for his memory and that he forgot nothing.
Source: al-Tabrisi, al-Ihtijaj, vol.1, p.281
Speaker: Imam Ali ﵇, in the report of Ishaq ibn Musa from Imam al-Kazim ﵇
Claim: Ali ﵇ gathered the Qur'an after the Prophet's ﷺ burial and the people refused it

Imam Ali ﵇ says he gathered the Qur'an after burying the Prophet ﷺ and the people refused it. The report of Salim ibn Salama gives the same refusal. Neither report says how Ali's ﵇ copy differed. Al-Mufid inclines to the view that the removed material was Ali's ﵇ interpretation. Al-Tabataba'i places any difference in the order of suras or of some verses.
Source: Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 176, p.252, and sermon 156, p.219, Subhi Salih numbering
Speaker: Imam Ali ﵇, without an isnad
Claim: this Qur'an guides without misleading, and the Book of God is the firm rope

Sermon 176 calls "this Qur'an" an adviser who does not deceive and a guide who does not lead astray. Sermon 156 tells its hearers to hold fast to the Book of God as the firm rope. Nahj al-Balagha gives both sermons without a chain of transmission.
Ali's Reading in the Printed Mushaf
Source: al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208
Speaker: Asim and Hafs ibn Sulayman, as reported by al-Dhahabi (d.748 AH)
Claim: Hafs read through Asim and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami to Ali ﵇

Asim says he never departed from al-Sulami's reading, and al-Sulami never departed from Ali's ﵇. Asim taught Hafs the reading he had recited to al-Sulami. He taught Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, known as Shu'ba, the reading he had presented to Zirr ibn Hubaysh from Ibn Mas'ud. By these reports, the Hafs reading descends through al-Sulami from Ali ﵇.
The introduction to the Cairo printing of the Qur'an, quoted by al-Tabrizi, says the printing follows Hafs from Asim. It traces Asim's reading through al-Sulami to four Companions, Ali ﵇ among them.
Source: Ibn Mihran, al-Mabsut fi al-Qira'at al-Ashr, p.440; al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, vol.2, p.183
Speaker: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash; al-Shawkani
Claim: readings from Ali ﵇ survive inside the canonical readings

Shu'ba says he brought ten readings from Ali's ﵇ reading into his reading of Asim. One of them is 'arafa with a light ra in Qur'an 66:3. The printed text of al-Mabsut gives both readings the same vocalization, including the doubling mark, so only Ibn Mihran's words "light" and "doubled" tell them apart. Al-Shawkani reports that Hamza and al-Kisa'i read faraqu in Qur'an 6:159, and he names it Ali's ﵇ reading. These reports place readings attributed to Ali ﵇ inside the canonical readings of Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i.
Collection in the Imami Sources
Source: al-Majlisi, Bihar al-Anwar, vol.89, pp.77-78, quoting al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi through Jami' al-Usul
Speaker: Zayd ibn Thabit
Claim: Zayd gathered the Qur'an for Abu Bakr from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones and the memories of men
Al-Majlisi's Bihar al-Anwar carries the Sunni account of how the Qur'an was collected. He copied Zayd ibn Thabit's report and labels it as al-Bukhari's and al-Tirmidhi's.

In Zayd's account, the killing on the day of Yamama has been heavy among the Qur'an reciters. Umar fears that much of the Qur'an will be lost and urges Abu Bakr to collect it. Abu Bakr then asks Zayd to gather the Qur'an. He gathers it from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones and men's memories. A narrator glosses the word for thin stones, lakhaf, as pottery.

Al-Askari cites Musnad Ahmad, where Ibn Abbas reports Uthman's account. The Prophet ﷺ told his scribes to place each revealed verse in a named sura. By this report, the Prophet ﷺ assigned verses to their suras.
Source: Ibn Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Masahif, p.67, no.39
Speaker: Imam Ali ﵇, through Suwayd ibn Ghafala
Claim: had Uthman not done it with the codices, Ali ﵇ would have

Suwayd ibn Ghafala reports that Ali ﵇ said of the codices, "If Uthman had not done it, I would have done it." Ibn Abi Dawud notes that Abu Dawud's version of the chain has an unnamed man before Suwayd. If the report is sound, Ali's ﵇ words endorse Uthman's unification of the codices.
The Earliest Manuscripts
Source: University of Birmingham news release, 22 July 2015; van Putten, BSOAS 82 (2019), pp.271-288; Sadeghi and Bergmann, Arabica 57 (2010), pp.343-436
Speaker: the University of Birmingham; Marijn van Putten; Behnam Sadeghi and Uwe Bergmann
Claim: the earliest dated copies fall close to the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime, and van Putten argues that fourteen early manuscripts descend from one written archetype

Radiocarbon analysis dated the parchment of the two Birmingham leaves to between 568 and 645 CE, with 95.4 per cent accuracy. The leaves carry parts of suras 18 to 20 in Hijazi, an early form of Arabic script. Marijn van Putten examined how fourteen early manuscripts spell ni'mat in the phrase "the grace of God". Each manuscript uses the same one of two possible spellings at the same places. He argues that only a single written archetype explains this agreement. On his argument, a project to codify the text took place in the first Islamic century. Sadeghi and Bergmann describe a manuscript from the first half of the seventh century CE. Its text does not belong to the Uthmanic tradition. They report it as the only known manuscript of that kind. These studies support an early written standard text. They do not show what the Companions' earlier copies contained.
The Scholars of the School
Source: al-Saduq, al-I'tiqadat, p.86
Speaker: Shaykh al-Saduq (d.381 AH)
Claim: the Qur'an is what lies between the two covers, and whoever attributes more to the Imamis lies

Al-Saduq's creed says the Qur'an God sent down is what lies between the two covers, and no more. He gives the people's count of suras as 114. He adds that the Imamis count al-Duha with al-Sharh, and al-Fil with Quraysh, as single suras. That ruling changes the count of suras and leaves the text the same.
Source: al-Mufid, al-Masa'il al-Sarawiyya, pp.78-79 and p.81; Awa'il al-Maqalat, pp.82-83
Speaker: Shaykh al-Mufid (d.413 AH)
Claim: al-Mufid gave two answers on omission, and in Awa'il al-Maqalat he inclined to the view that only interpretation was removed

In al-Sarawiyya al-Mufid says everything between the covers is God's speech and the majority of what was sent down. He says the rest is with the guardian of the law, who is entrusted with the rulings, and none of it is lost. He names three reasons the compiler left it out, namely limited knowledge, doubt and deliberate exclusion. He adds that the Imams ﵈ commanded recitation of what lies between the covers until al-Qa'im ﵇ rises.

In Awa'il al-Maqalat al-Mufid says reason allows omission. He found no argument against it that he could rely on. He reports a group of Imamis who deny the loss of any word, verse or sura. They hold that what was removed was the interpretation recorded in Ali's ﵇ codex. Al-Mufid calls their view closer to the truth and inclines toward it. He rules out the addition of a sura's length, and he allows that a word or a letter could be added. He says that God would make any such addition known, and he inclines to deny that it occurred. The sources quoted give no order in which al-Mufid wrote the two works.
Source: al-Murtada, al-Dhakhira fi Ilm al-Kalam, pp.361-362; al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, vol.1, pp.42-43
Speaker: al-Sharif al-Murtada (d.436 AH); Amin al-Islam al-Tabrisi (d.548 AH)
Claim: knowledge of the Qur'an's transmission is like knowledge of great cities and events

Al-Murtada answers an objector who says the Imamis, like the hashwiyya among the traditionists, claim change and loss in the Qur'an. Hashwiyya is the name the objector gives to a group among the hadith folk. Al-Murtada says knowledge of the Qur'an's transmission is like knowledge of great cities and famous events. He adds that the theologians among the scholars knew everything disputed in it, including its inflection and its readings. He asks how the Qur'an could be altered or diminished under such care.
In the introduction to Majma' al-Bayan, al-Tabrisi sets aside the discussion of addition to and loss from the Qur'an as unsuitable for exegesis.

Al-Tabrisi calls addition invalid by consensus. He reports that some Imamis, and a band of the hashwiyya among the general body of Muslims, narrated loss. He calls the denial of loss the sound position of his school. His passage reports the loss view without naming the scholars who held it.
Source: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.259
Speaker: al-Khoei
Claim: the claim of tahrif is a fable

Al-Khoei closes his discussion by calling tahrif a fable. He says only a weak or unreflecting mind holds it, or one whom love of the view drives to it. The printed al-Bayan reads yajib, "must", at that point. Other works that quote the passage read hubb, "love", which matches al-Khoei's next sentence, "Love blinds and deafens".
Source: al-Khomeini, Anwar al-Hidaya fi al-Ta'liqa ala al-Kifaya, vol.1, pp.207-208
Speaker: Sayyid Ruhollah al-Khomeini (d.1409 AH)
Claim: the verifying scholars of both groups deny tahrif, and Fasl al-Khitab cites reports the early scholars had set aside

Al-Khomeini says the verifying scholars among the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) and among the particular group (al-khassa), meaning the Shia, deny tahrif. He says Fasl al-Khitab, al-Nuri's collection of reports on tahrif, cites reports that the associates (al-ashab, the school's scholars) turned away from. He adds that early scholars such as the three Muhammads had already cleared the reports of such weak items. Imami scholars give that name to al-Kulayni, al-Saduq and al-Tusi. He calls al-Nuri righteous and diligent, and too eager for weak and strange material. On the next page he tests the claim of the author of Fasl al-Khitab "and his like" against the history of the dispute over succession. Suppose the Book were full of the Household's merits and of Ali's ﵇ appointment. He asks why Ali ﵇, Fatimah ﵍, al-Hasan ﵇ and al-Husayn ﵇ never argued from those verses. He asks the same of Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad and Ammar. He also asks why Ali ﵇ relied on the Prophet's ﷺ hadiths while the Qur'an was among them.

Al-Sistani is asked about internet claims that attribute tahrif to the Shia. He calls the claim false. He says the Qur'an God sent down is the Qur'an Muslims have today, without addition or deficiency.
Source: al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, pp.52-58
Speaker: al-Fayd al-Kashani (d.1091 AH)
Claim: the reports show the Qur'an in hand is incomplete, and the whole survives with its people

Al-Fayd reads the reports as showing that the Qur'an in hand is incomplete, partly altered and out of order. He counts Ali's ﵇ name among the things removed. He lists three objections to that reading. No verse could be relied on, and Qur'an 15:9 and 41:42 would be contradicted. Qur'an 41:42 says falsehood cannot reach the Book. The rule of judging reports by the Book would also lose its use. He allows that some omitted material was explanation, so that "it was revealed thus" gives the intended sense. He concludes that the whole Qur'an exists, preserved with "its people" (ahlihi), a phrase for which he names no group. The part the community needs is in its hands, even if it cannot reach the rest. He likens the Qur'an to the Imam, who also exists beyond the community's reach. Al-Mufid's Sarawiyya places the rest of the revelation with the guardian of the law, which resembles this answer.
Glossary
shawadhdh. Irregular readings, reported outside the accepted readings.
tanzil. Revelation, the act of sending down or the text sent down. Al-Tabataba'i reads "it was revealed thus" in many reports as the explanation that accompanied the revelation.
kuttab. Plural of katib, writer or scribe.
Final Verdict
Final Verdict

Imami scholars from al-Saduq to al-Sistani hold that the Qur'an between the two covers is the Qur'an God sent down. Al-Majlisi and al-Fayd al-Kashani read some reports as evidence of loss, and al-Mufid allows omission by the compiler. These positions show that some Imami scholars accepted or allowed omission. They do not make alteration the doctrine of the Imamiyya.

quotes.caption: Ibn Hazm, al-Fisal, vol.4, p.182

paragraphs.text: ومن قول الإمامية كلها قديما وحديثا ان القرآن مبدل زيد فيه ما ليس منه ونقص منه كثير وبدل منه كثير حاشا علي ابن الحسن ابن موسى بن محمد بن إبراهيم بن موسى بن جعفر بن محمد بن علي بن الحسن ابن علي بن أبي طالب وكان أماميا يظاهر بالاعتزال مع ذلك فإنه كان ينكر هذا القول ويكفر من قاله وكذلك صاحباه أبو يعلى ميلاد الطوسي وأبو القاسم الرازي

It is the view of all the Imamites, early and late, that the Qur'an has been altered, that material not part of it was added to it, and that much was removed from it and much was changed in it. The one exception is Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib. He was an Imamite who openly sided with Mu'tazilism, and yet he rejected this view and declared anyone who held it an unbeliever. His two companions, Abu Yala Milad al-Tusi and Abu al-Qasim al-Razi, did the same.

quotes.caption: al-Safadi, al-Wafi bil-Wafayat, vol.21, pp.2-3

paragraphs.text: الشريف المرتضى علي بن الحسين بين موسى بن محمد بن موسى بن إبراهيم بن موسى بن جعفر بن محمد بن علي بن الحسين بن علي بن أبي طالب أبو القاسم المرتضى علم الهدى نقيب العلويين أخو الشريف الرضي ولد سنة خمس وخمسين وثلاث مائة وتوفي سنة ست وثلاثين وأربع مائة وكان فاضلا ماهرا أديبا متكلما له مصنفات جمة على مذهب الشيعة قال الخطيب كتبت عنه وكان رأسا في الاعتزال كثير الاطلاع والجدال قال ابن حزم في الملل والنحل ومن قول الإمامية كلها قديما وحديثا أن القرآن مبدل زيد فيه ونقص منه حاشا علي بن الحسين بن موسى وكان إماميا فيه تظاهر بالاعتزال ومع ذلك فإنه كان ينكر هذا) القول وكفر من قاله وكذلك صاحباه أبو يعلى الطوسي وأبو القاسم الرازي

Al-Sharif al-Murtada Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu al-Qasim al-Murtada, Alam al-Huda, was the marshal (naqib) of the Alawids, the descendants of Ali, and the brother of al-Sharif al-Radi. He was born in the year 355 and died in the year 436. He was a distinguished and skilled scholar, a man of letters and a theologian, and he wrote many works according to the doctrine of the Shia. Al-Khatib said, "I wrote down reports from him. He was a leader in the Mutazilite school, with wide learning and a great deal of debate." Ibn Hazm said in al-Milal wa-l-Nihal, "It is the position of all the Imamis, past and present, that the Quran has been altered, that something was added to it and something was removed from it, except Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa. He was an Imami who made a show of Mutazilism. Even so, he rejected this claim and declared anyone who made it to be an unbeliever. So did his two companions, Abu Yala al-Tusi and Abu al-Qasim al-Razi."

quotes.caption: al-Jawhari, al-Sihah, vol.4, p.31

paragraphs.text: وتحريف الكلام عن مواضعه : تغييره . وتحريف القلم : قطه محرفا . ويقال : انحرف عنه وتحرف واحرورف ، أي مال وعدل .

Tahrif of speech from its places means changing it. Tahrif of the pen means cutting it at a slant. One says “inharafa from him,” “taharrafa,” and “ihrawrafa,” meaning that he inclined away and turned aside.

quotes.caption: Ibn Manzur, Lisan al-Arab, vol.9, p.43

paragraphs.text: وتَحْرِيفُ الكَلِم عن مواضِعِه : تغييره . والتحريف في القرآن والكلمة : تغيير الحرفِ عن معناه والكلمة عن معناها وهي قريبة الشبه كما كانت اليهود تُغَيِّرُ مَعانَي التوراة بالأَشباه ، فوصَفَهم اللَّه بفعلهم فقال تعالى : يُحَرِّفُون الكَلِمَ عن مواضعه .

To distort words away from their places is to change them. Distortion in the Qur'an and in a word means changing a letter away from its meaning, or a word away from its meaning, while keeping a close resemblance to it. The Jews used to change the meanings of the Torah in this way, by means of look-alikes. God described them by their deed in His words, "They distort words from their places."

quotes.caption: Qur'an 4:46

paragraphs.text: مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَٱسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍۢ وَرَٰعِنَا لَيًّۢا بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَطَعْنًۭا فِى ٱلدِّينِ ۚ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا وَٱسْمَعْ وَٱنظُرْنَا لَكَانَ خَيْرًۭا لَّهُمْ وَأَقْوَمَ وَلَٰكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا

mina alladhina hadu yuharrifuna al-kalima 'an mawadi'ihi wa-yaquluna sami'na wa-'asayna wa-isma' ghayra musma'in wa-ra'ina layyan bi-alsinatihim wa-ta'nan fi al-din, wa-law annahum qalu sami'na wa-ata'na wa-isma' wa-unzurna la-kana khayran lahum wa-aqwama wa-lakin la'anahumu Allahu bi-kufrihim fa-la yu'minuna illa qalilan

Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their proper places. They say, “We hear and we disobey,” and “Hear, without being made to hear,” and “Ra'ina,” twisting their tongues and slandering the religion. Had they said, “We hear and we obey,” and “Hear,” and “Look at us,” it would have been better for them and more upright. But God has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little.

quotes.caption: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.197

paragraphs.text: 1 - معنى التحريف : يطلق لفظ التحريف ويراد منه عدة معان على سبيل الاشتراك ، فبعض منها واقع في القرآن باتفاق من المسلمين ، وبعض منها لم يقع فيه باتفاق منهم أيضا ، وبعض منها وقع الخلاف بينهم . واليك تفصيل ذلك (1) : الأول : " نقل الشئ عن موضعه وتحويله إلى غيره " ومنه قوله تعالى : " من الذين هادوا يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه 4 : 46 " . ولا خلاف بين المسلمين في وقوع مثل هذا التحريف في كتاب الله فإن كل من فسر القرآن بغير حقيقته ، وحمله على غير معناه فقد حرفه . وترى كثيرا من أهل البدع ، والمذاهب الفاسدة قد حرفوا القرآن بتأويلهم آياته على آرائهم وأهوائهم . وقد ورد المنع عن التحريف بهذا المعنى ، وذم فاعله في عدة من الروايات .

1. The meaning of tahrif. The word tahrif is used for several meanings as a shared term. Some of these meanings occur in the Qur'an by the agreement of the Muslims, some do not occur in it, also by their agreement, and about some of them the Muslims disagree. Here are the details.

The first meaning is “moving a thing from its place and turning it into something else.” To this belongs the saying of the Exalted, “Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their places” 4:46. There is no disagreement among the Muslims that this kind of tahrif occurs in the Book of God. Anyone who explains the Qur'an other than according to its reality, and applies it to a meaning other than its own, has distorted it. You will see many people of innovation and of corrupt schools who have distorted the Qur'an by interpreting its verses to fit their own opinions and desires. The prohibition of tahrif in this sense, and the condemnation of the one who does it, have come down in a number of reports.

quotes.caption: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.200

paragraphs.text: الخامس : " التحريف بالزيادة بمعنى أن بعض المصحف الذي بأيدينا ليس من الكلام المنزل " . والتحريف بهذا المعنى باطل بإجماع المسلمين ، بل هو مما علم بطلانه بالضرورة . السادس : " التحريف بالنقيصة ، بمعنى أن المصحف الذي بأيدينا لا يشتمل على جميع القرآن الذي نزل من السماء ، فقد ضاع بعضه على الناس " . والتحريف بهذا المعنى هو الذي وقع فيه الخلاف فأثبته قوم ونفاه آخرون .

The fifth meaning is “tahrif by addition, meaning that part of the codex in our hands is not part of the revealed speech.” Tahrif in this sense is false by the consensus of the Muslims. Its falsity is in fact known by necessity.

The sixth meaning is “tahrif by omission, meaning that the codex in our hands does not contain all of the Qur'an that was sent down from heaven, so that some of it was lost to the people.” This is the sense of tahrif about which the disagreement occurred. One group affirmed it and others denied it.

quotes.caption: Qur'an 15:9

paragraphs.text: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
inna nahnu nazzalna al-dhikra wa-inna lahu la-hafizun
Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians.

quotes.caption: al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, vol.12, p.107

paragraphs.text: فقد تبين مما فصلناه ان القرآن الذي أنزله الله على نبيه ﵌ ووصفه بأنه ذكر محفوظ على ما انزل مصون بصيانة الهية عن الزيادة والنقيصة والتغيير كما وعد الله نبيه فيه . وخلاصة الحجة ان القرآن أنزله الله على نبيه ووصفه في آيات كثيرة بأوصاف خاصة لو كان تغير في شئ من هذه الأوصاف بزيادة أو نقيصة أو تغيير في لفظ أو ترتيب مؤثر فقد آثار تلك الصفة قطعا لكنا نجد القرآن الذي بأيدينا واجدا لاثار تلك الصفات المعدودة على أتم ما يمكن وأحسن ما يكون فلم يقع فيه تحريف يسلبه شيئا من صفاته فالذي بأيدينا منه هو القرآن المنزل على النبي ﵌ بعينه فلو فرض سقوط شئ منه أو تغير في اعراب أو حرف أو ترتيب وجب ان يكون في أمر لا يؤثر في شئ من أوصافه كالاعجاز وارتفاع الاختلاف والهداية والنورية والذكرية والهيمنة على سائر الكتب السماوية إلى غير ذلك وذلك كآية مكررة ساقطة أو اختلاف في نقطة أو اعراب ونحوها .

What we have set out shows that the Qur'an which God sent down to his Prophet, and which he described as a preserved Reminder, remains as it was sent down. It is protected by divine safeguarding from addition, omission and alteration, as God promised his Prophet in it.

The summary of the argument is this. God sent the Qur'an down to his Prophet and described it in many verses with particular attributes. If any of these attributes had changed through addition, omission, or a change in a word or in an order that affects it, the traces of that attribute would certainly have been affected. Yet we find that the Qur'an in our hands carries the traces of those enumerated attributes to the fullest extent possible and in the best form. So no tahrif has occurred in it that strips it of any of its attributes. What we have of it is therefore the very Qur'an that was sent down to the Prophet.

If we suppose that something dropped out of it, or that a vowel ending, a letter or an order changed, then it must have been in a matter that affects none of its attributes. Those attributes include its inimitability, the absence of discrepancy in it, its guidance, its luminosity, its being a reminder, and its authority over the other heavenly books, and so on. An example is a repeated verse that dropped out, or a difference in a dot or a vowel ending, and the like.

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.634, no.28

paragraphs.text: 28 - علي بن الحكم ، عن هشام بن سالم (2) ، عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : إن القرآن الذي جاء به جبرئيل (﵇) إلى محمد (﵌) سبعة عشر ألف آية (3) .
28. Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abd Allah, who said.
“The Qur'an that Gabriel brought to Muhammad was seventeen thousand verses.”

quotes.caption: al-Saduq, al-I'tiqadat, pp.86-87

paragraphs.text: بل نقول : إنه قد نزل الوحي الذي ليس بقرآن ، ما لو جمع إلى القرآن لكان مبلغه مقدار سبعة عشر ألف آية .
We say, moreover, that revelation has come down that is not Qur'an, and that if it were gathered together with the Qur'an, its total would amount to seventeen thousand verses.

quotes.caption: al-Majlisi in al-Milani, al-Tahqiq fi Nafy al-Tahrif, pp.86-88

paragraphs.text: 2 - الشيخ المجلسي في كتابه ( مرآة العقول ) فإنّه قال بعد حديث قال إنّه موثق : « ولا يخفى أنّ هذا الخبر وكثير من الأخبار الصحيحة صريحة في نقص القرآن وتغييره . وعندي أنّ الأخبار في هذا الباب متواترة معنىً ، وطرح جميعها يوجب رفع الاعتماد على الأخبار رأساً ، بل ظنّي أنّ الأخبار في هذا الباب لا تقصر عن أخبار الإمامة ، فكيف يثبتونها بالخبر » . ويردّه ما ذكره هو في « بحار الأنوار » وقد تقدّم نصّة . على أنّ قوله : « وكثير من الأخبار الصحيحة صريحة في نقص القرآن » غريب ، فإنّ السيد المرتضى قال : « نقلوا أخباراً ضعيفة ظنّوا صحتها لا يرجع بمثلها عن المعلوم المقطوع على صحته » . كما أنكر صحتها الطوسي شيخ الطائفة والمحدّث الكاشاني ، بل جاء في العبارة التي نقلناها عن بحاره « إنّ الأخبار التي جاءت بذلك أخبار آحاد لا يقطع على الله تعالى بصحّتها » . ومن قبلهم قال شيخ المحدّثين ما نصّه : « إعتقادنا أنّ القرآن الذين أنزله الله على نبيّه ﵌ هو ما بين الدفّتين وما في أيدي الناس ، ليس بأكثر من ذاك . . . ومن نسب إلينا أنّا نقول إنّه أكثر من ذلك فهو كاذب » . ولو كانت أحاديث النقيصة صحيحة ومقبولة لما قال الصدوق ذلك كما لا يخفى . وأما قوله : « وطرح جميعها يوجب رفع الاعتماد على الأخبار رأساً » ففيه : إنّ قبول جميعها أيضاً يوجب رفع الاعتماد على الأحاديث رأساً ، على أنّه رحمة الله قد حكم في أكثر الأحاديث المخرّجة في « الكافي » والمفيدة نقص القرآن إمّا بالضعف وإمّا بالإرسال ، كما تقدّم ذلك كلّه . ومن العجيب قوله : « بل ظنّي . . . » إذ إثبات الإمامية ليس دليلة منحصراً بالأحاديث حتى يقال ذلك ، وكيف أنّ تلك الأحاديث لا تقصر عن أحاديث الإمامة ؟ وهل يقصد الكثرة في الورود ؟ أو القوة في الدلالة ؟ أو الصحة في الأسانيد ؟

2. Al-Shaykh al-Majlisi, in his book Mir'at al-'Uqul, said after a hadith that he called reliable, "It is not hidden that this report and many sound reports are explicit about the diminution and alteration of the Quran. In my view the reports on this subject are mutawatir in meaning, and rejecting all of them would remove reliance on reports altogether. Rather, I think the reports on this subject fall no shorter than the reports on the Imamate, so how can they establish the Imamate by a report?" What he himself mentioned in Bihar al-Anwar refutes this, and its text has already been given.

Moreover, his statement "many sound reports are explicit about the diminution of the Quran" is strange, because al-Sayyid al-Murtada said, "They transmitted weak reports that they thought were sound, and one does not turn away from what is known and certain to be sound because of the like of these." Al-Tusi, the Shaykh of the sect, and the hadith scholar al-Kashani likewise denied their soundness. Indeed, the passage we quoted from his Bihar says, "The reports that came about this are solitary reports (ahad), and their soundness cannot be affirmed with certainty about God Most High." Before them, the Shaykh of the hadith scholars said, in these words, "Our belief is that the Quran which God sent down to His Prophet is what is between the two covers and in the hands of the people, and it is no more than that... Whoever attributes to us that we say it is more than that is a liar." Had the hadiths of diminution been sound and accepted, al-Saduq would not have said this, as is clear.

As for his statement "rejecting all of them would remove reliance on reports altogether," the reply is that accepting all of them would also remove reliance on hadiths altogether. Moreover, may God have mercy on him, he judged most of the hadiths cited in al-Kafi that indicate diminution of the Quran to be either weak or mursal, as all of that has been shown earlier. His statement "Rather, I think..." is also remarkable, since the proof of the Imamate is not confined to hadiths, so that this could be said. And how do those hadiths fall no shorter than the hadiths of the Imamate? Does he mean abundance in transmission, strength in indication, or soundness in the chains of transmission?

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.633, no.23

paragraphs.text: 23 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن محمد بن الحسين ، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي هاشم ، عن سالم بن سلمة قال : قرأ رجل على أبي عبد الله (﵇) وأنا أستمع حروفا من القرآن ليس على ما يقرؤها الناس ، فقال أبو عبد الله (﵇) : كف عن هذه القراءة اقرأ كما يقرأ الناس حتى يقوم القائم فإذا قام القائم (﵇) قرأ كتاب الله ﷿ على حده وأخرج المصحف الذي كتبه علي (﵇) وقال : أخرجه علي (﵇) إلى الناس حين فرغ منه وكتبه فقال لهم : هذا كتاب الله ﷿ كما أنزله [الله] على محمد (﵌) وقد جمعته من اللوحين فقالوا : هو ذا عندنا مصحف جامع فيه القرآن لا حاجة لنا فيه ، فقال أما والله ما ترونه بعد يومكم هذا أبدا ، إنما كان علي أن أخبركم حين جمعته لتقرؤوه .
23. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Salama, who said.

A man recited to Abu Abd Allah, while I was listening, some letters of the Qur'an that were not as the people recite them. Abu Abd Allah said, “Stop this recitation. Recite as the people recite until the Qa'im rises. When the Qa'im rises, he will recite the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, by itself, and he will bring out the codex that Ali wrote.”

And he said, “Ali brought it out to the people when he had finished it and written it. He said to them, ‘This is the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, as [God] sent it down to Muhammad, and I have gathered it from the two tablets.’ They said, ‘Here with us is a codex that contains the whole Qur'an, and we have no need of it.’ He said, ‘By God, you will never see it after this day of yours. It was only my duty to inform you, when I had gathered it, so that you would recite it.’”

quotes.caption: Imam al-Baqir, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.228, no.1

paragraphs.text: (باب) (انه لم يجمع القرآن كله الا الأئمة ﵈ وانهم) (يعلمون علمه كله) 1 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن ابن محبوب ، عن عمرو بن أبي المقدام عن جابر قال : سمعت أبا جعفر ﵇ يقول : ما ادعى أحد من الناس أنه جمع القرآن كله كما أنزل إلا كذاب ، وما جمعه وحفظه كما نزله الله تعالى إلا علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ والأئمة من بعده ﵈ .
Chapter. That no one collected the whole Quran except the Imams, and that they know all of its knowledge.
1 - Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, who said that he heard Abu Ja'far say,

“No one among the people claims that he collected the whole Quran as it was sent down, except a liar. No one collected it and memorized it as God Most High sent it down except Ali ibn Abi Talib and the Imams after him.”

quotes.caption: Jabir, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.417, no.26

paragraphs.text: 26 - وبهذا الاسناد ، عن محمد بن سنان ، عن عمار بن مروان ، عن منخل ، عن جابر ، قال : نزل جبرئيل ﵇ بهذه الآية على محمد هكذا : " وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا (في علي) فأتوا بسورة من مثله (3) " .
26 - Through this same chain, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Munakhkhal, from Jabir, who said,
Gabriel came down to Muhammad with this verse in this form, “If you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant (concerning Ali), then bring a surah like it.”

quotes.caption: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.226

paragraphs.text: والجواب : أن هذه الروايات لا دلالة فيها على وقوع التحريف في القرآن بالمعنى المتنازع فيه ، وتوضيح ذلك : أن كثيرا من الروايات ، وإن كانت ضعيفة السند ، فإن جملة منها نقلت من كتاب أحمد بن محمد السياري ، الذي اتفق علماء الرجال على فساد مذهبه ، وأنه يقول بالتناسخ ، ومن علي بن أحمد الكوفي الذي ذكر علماء الرجال أنه كذاب ، وأنه فاسد المذهب إلا أن كثرة الروايات تورث القطع بصدور بعضها عن المعصومين ﵈ ولا أقل من الاطمئنان بذلك ، وفيها ما روي بطريق معتبر فلا حاجة بنا إلى التكلم في سند كل رواية بخصوصها .

The answer is that these reports give no indication that distortion occurred in the Quran in the sense under dispute. To explain this, many of the reports have weak chains of transmission. A number of them were transmitted from the book of Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari, whose doctrine the scholars of biographical evaluation agreed was corrupt, and who held the belief in transmigration of souls. Others were transmitted from Ali ibn Ahmad al-Kufi, whom the scholars of biographical evaluation described as a liar with a corrupt doctrine. Nevertheless, the large number of reports produces certainty that some of them were issued by the infallible Imams, and at the very least it produces confidence in that. Among them are reports narrated through a reliable route. So we have no need to discuss the chain of each report individually.

quotes.caption: al-Muhammadi, Salamat al-Qur'an min al-Tahrif, p.120

paragraphs.text: لأن مجموع الروايات التي نقلها المحدث النوري - ويزعم أنها اختصت بكتب الإمامية - يصل إلى 1602 رواية موزعة على النحو الآتي : * 350 رواية ( يعنى حدود ثلث الروايات التي جمعها ) من كتاب القراءات لأحمد بن محمد السياري ، وهذا الكتاب لا قيمة له عند الإمامية ومؤلفه ضعيف الحديث عند الفريقين (2) .

The total of the reports that the hadith scholar al-Nuri transmitted, which he claims are particular to the books of the Imamis, reaches 1602 reports, distributed as follows. There are 350 reports, meaning about a third of the reports he collected, from the Book of Recitations by Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari. This book has no value among the Imamis, and its author is weak in hadith according to both groups.

quotes.caption: al-Najashi in al-Khoei, Mu'jam Rijal al-Hadith, vol.3, p.71

paragraphs.text: 874 - أحمد بن محمد بن سيار : = أحمد بن محمد البصري . = أحمد بن محمد السياري . قال النجاشي : " أحمد بن محمد بن سيار أبو عبد الله الكاتب بصري ، كان من كتاب آل طاهر ، في زمن أبي محمد ﵇ ، ويعرف بالسياري ، ضعيف الحديث ، فاسد المذهب - ذكر ذلك لنا : الحسين بن عبيد الله - مجفو الرواية ، كثير المراسيل ، له كتب ، وقع إلينا منها : كتاب ثواب القرآن ، كتاب الطب ، كتاب القراءات ، كتاب النوادر ، كتاب الغارات ، أخبرنا الحسين بن عبيد الله ، قال : حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن يحيى ، عن أبيه ، قال : حدثني السياري ، إلا ما كان من غلو وتخليط " .

874. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar, who is also Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Basri and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari. Al-Najashi said, "Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar, Abu Abd Allah the scribe, was from Basra. He was one of the secretaries of the Al Tahir in the time of Abu Muhammad, and he is known as al-Sayyari. He is weak in hadith and corrupt in doctrine, as al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah told us. His transmission is shunned, and he has many mursal reports. He has books, of which these reached us. The Book of the Reward of the Quran, the Book of Medicine, the Book of Recitations, the Book of Rare Reports, and the Book of the Raids. Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah informed us and said, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us from his father, who said, al-Sayyari narrated to me, except for what contained exaggeration (ghuluw) and confusion."

quotes.caption: al-Tusi, al-Tibyan, vol.1, p.77

paragraphs.text: وأما الكلام في زيادته ونقصانه فمما لا يليق به أيضا ، لان الزيادة فيه مجمع على بطلانها والنقصان منه ، فالظاهر أيضا من مذهب المسلمين خلافه ، وهو الأليق بالصحيح من مذهبنا وهو الذي نصره المرتضى (ره) ، وهو الظاهر في الروايات غير أنه رويت روايات كثيره ، من جهة الخاصة والعامة ، بنقصان كثير من آي القرآن ، ونقل شئ منه من موضع إلى موضع ، طريقها الآحاد التي لا توجب علما ولا عملا ، والأولى الاعراض عنها ، وترك التشاغل بها ، لأنه يمكن تأويلها ولو صحت لما كان ذلك طعنا على ما هو موجود بين الدفتين ، فان ذلك معلوم صحته ، لا يعترضه أحد من الأمة ولا يدفعه ورواياتنا متناصرة بالحث على قراءته والتمسك بما فيه ، ورد ما يرد من اختلاف الاخبار في الفروع إليه .

The discussion of the Quran's increase and decrease is also unsuitable here. Increase in it is unanimously held to be invalid. As for decrease from it, the apparent position of the Muslims is the opposite. That is also the view more fitting for the sound position of our school, and it is the view that al-Murtada, may God have mercy on him, supported, and it is the apparent meaning of the reports.

Nevertheless, many reports have been narrated, from our own side (al-khassa) and from the general body of Muslims (al-'amma), that many verses of the Quran were diminished and that some of it was moved from one place to another. These reports come by solitary chains (ahad), which establish neither knowledge nor practice. It is better to turn away from them and to leave off occupying oneself with them, because they can be interpreted. Even if they were sound, that would not be a criticism of what exists between the two covers, because the soundness of that is known, no one in the community objects to it, and no one rejects it. Our reports agree in urging its recitation and holding fast to what is in it, and in referring back to it whatever differences arise among the reports on matters of detail.

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.69, no.5

paragraphs.text: 5 - محمد بن إسماعيل ، عن الفضل بن شاذان ، عن ابن أبي عمير ، عن هشام بن الحكم وغيره ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : خطب النبي ﵌ بمنى فقال : أيها الناس ما جاء كم عني يوافق كتاب الله فأنا قلته وما جاء كم يخالف كتاب الله فلم أقله .
5 - Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and others, from Abu Abd Allah, who said,

The Prophet gave a sermon at Mina and said, “O people, whatever comes to you from me that agrees with the Book of God, I said it. Whatever comes to you that contradicts the Book of God, I did not say it.”

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, Wasa'il al-Shi'a, vol.27, p.118, no.33362

paragraphs.text: (33362) 29 - سعيد بن هبة الله الراوندي في (رسالته) التي ألفها في أحوال أحاديث أصحابنا وإثبات صحتها ، عن محمد ، وعلي ابني علي بن عبد الصمد ، عن أبيهما ، عن أبي البركات علي بن الحسين ، عن أبي جعفر ابن بابويه ، عن أبيه ، عن سعد بن عبد الله عن أيوب بن نوح ، عن محمد ابن أبي عمير ، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عبد الله قال : قال الصادق (﵇) : إذا ورد عليكم حديثان مختلفان فاعرضوهما على كتاب الله ، فما وافق كتاب الله فخذوه ، وما خالف كتاب الله فردوه ، فإن لم تجدوهما في كتاب الله فاعرضوهما على أخبار العامة ، فما وافق أخبارهم فذروه ، وما خالف أخبراهم فخذوه .

(33362) 29. Sa'id ibn Hibat Allah al-Rawandi, in his treatise that he wrote on the conditions of the hadiths of our companions and the proof of their soundness, from Muhammad and Ali, the two sons of Ali ibn Abd al-Samad, from their father, from Abu al-Barakat Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abd Allah, who said.

Al-Sadiq said, "When two differing hadiths reach you, present them to the Book of God. Take what agrees with the Book of God and reject what contradicts the Book of God. If you do not find them in the Book of God, present them to the reports of the general body of Muslims (al-'amma). Leave what agrees with their reports, and take what contradicts their reports."

quotes.caption: Imam al-Baqir, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.630, no.12

paragraphs.text: 12 - الحسين بن محمد ، عن علي بن محمد ، عن الوشاء ، عن جميل بن دراج ، عن محمد بن مسلم ، عن زرارة ، عن أبي جعفر (﵇) قال : إن القرآن واحد نزل من عند واحد ولكن الاختلاف يجيئ من قبل الرواة .
12 - al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far, who said,
“The Quran is one, sent down from One. But the disagreement comes from the side of the transmitters.”

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.630, no.13

paragraphs.text: 13 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن أبيه ، عن ابن أبي عمير ، عن عمر بن أذينة ، عن الفضيل بن يسار قال : قلت لأبي عبد الله (﵇) : إن الناس يقولون : إن القرآن نزل على سبعة أحرف ، فقال : كذبوا أعداء الله ولكنه نزل على حرف واحد من عند الواحد (1) .
13 - Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said,
I said to Abu Abd Allah, “The people say that the Quran was sent down in seven ahruf.” He said, “The enemies of God have lied. Rather, it was sent down in one harf, from the One.”

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.631, no.15

paragraphs.text: 15 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن سهل بن زياد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، ، عن عبد الله ابن جندب ، عن سفيان بن السمط قال : سألت أبا عبد الله (﵇) : عن تنزيل القرآن قال : اقرؤوا كما علمتم .
15 - A group of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd Allah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samt, who said,
I asked Abu Abd Allah about the sending down of the Quran. He said, “Recite as you were taught.”

quotes.caption: Ibn Mas'ud, Musnad Abi Ya'la, vol.8, p.470, no.5057

paragraphs.text: (5057) حدثنا أبو كريب حدثنا أبو بكر بن عياش عن عاصم عن زر عن عبد الله قال اختصم رجلان في سورة فقال هذا أقرأني رسول الله ﵌ وقال هذا أقرأني رسول الله فأتيا النبي ﵌ فأخبر بذلك قال فتغير وجهه فقال إقرؤوا كما علمتم فذكر فيه كلاما ثم قال فإنما هلك من كان قبلكم باختلافهم على أنبيائهم
(5057) Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Asim, from Zirr, from Abd Allah, who said,

Two men disputed over a surah. One said, “The Messenger of God taught me to recite it,” and the other said, “The Messenger of God taught me to recite it.” They came to the Prophet and he was told of this. He said that his face changed, and he said, “Recite as you were taught.”
Then he mentioned some words about it, and then said, “Those before you were destroyed only because of their disagreement with their prophets.”

quotes.caption: al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, vol.12, p.108

paragraphs.text: وكذا الاخبار التي تتضمن تمسك أئمة أهل البيت ﵈ بمختلف الآيات القرآنية في كل باب على ما يوافق القرآن الموجود عندنا حتى في الموارد التي فيها آحاد من الروايات بالتحريف وهذا أحسن شاهد على أن المراد في كثير من روايات التحريف من قولهم ﵈ كذا نزل هو التفسير بحسب التنزيل في مقابل البطن والتأويل . وكذا الروايات الواردة عن أمير المؤمنين وسائر الأئمة من ذريته ﵈ في إن ما بأيدي الناس قرآن نازل من عند الله سبحانه وان كان غير ما الفه علي ﵇ من المصحف ولم يشركوه ﵇ في التأليف في زمن أبى بكر ولا في زمن عثمان ومن هذا الباب قولهم ﵈ لشيعتهم : اقرؤوا كما قرء الناس ومقتضى هذه الروايات ان لو كان القرآن الدائر بين الناس مخالفا لما الفه علي ﵇ في شئ فإنما يخالفه في ترتيب السور أو في ترتيب بعض الآيات التي لا يؤثر اختلال ترتيبها في مدلولها شيئا ولا في الأوصاف التي وصف الله سبحانه بها القرآن النازل من عنده ما يختل به آثارها . فمجموع هذه الروايات على اختلاف أصنافها يدل دلالة قاطعة على أن الذي بأيدينا من القرآن هو القرآن النازل على النبي ﵌ من غير أن يفقد شيئا من أوصافه الكريمة وآثارها وبركاتها .

Likewise there are the reports that include the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt holding to various Qur'anic verses on every subject, in agreement with the Qur'an we have, even in the cases where there are isolated reports of alteration. This is the best evidence that what is meant in many of the alteration reports, in their saying "It was revealed thus," is explanation according to the revelation, as distinct from the inner meaning and the interpretation.

Likewise there are the reports from the Commander of the Faithful and the rest of the Imams from his descendants, saying that what is in the people's hands is a Qur'an sent down from God, Glorified, even though it differs from the codex that Ali compiled, and that they did not involve him in the compilation, either in the time of Abu Bakr or in the time of Uthman. To this category belongs their saying to their Shia, "Recite as the people recite." The implication of these reports is that if the Qur'an circulating among the people differs in anything from what Ali compiled, it differs only in the order of the surahs, or in the order of some verses whose disordering has no effect on their meaning. It does not differ in the attributes with which God, Glorified, described the Qur'an sent down from Him, so as to impair their effects.

So these reports taken together, despite their different kinds, indicate conclusively that the Qur'an in our hands is the Qur'an sent down upon the Prophet, without having lost any of its noble attributes, its effects, or its blessings.

quotes.caption: Qur'an 5:95

paragraphs.text: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلصَّيْدَ وَأَنتُمْ حُرُمٌۭ ۚ وَمَن قَتَلَهُۥ مِنكُم مُّتَعَمِّدًۭا فَجَزَآءٌۭ مِّثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ ٱلنَّعَمِ يَحْكُمُ بِهِۦ ذَوَا عَدْلٍۢ مِّنكُمْ هَدْيًۢا بَٰلِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ أَوْ كَفَّٰرَةٌۭ طَعَامُ مَسَٰكِينَ أَوْ عَدْلُ ذَٰلِكَ صِيَامًۭا لِّيَذُوقَ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِۦ ۗ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا سَلَفَ ۚ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنتَقِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنْهُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌۭ ذُو ٱنتِقَامٍ

ya ayyuha alladhina amanu la taqtulu al-sayda wa-antum hurumun, wa-man qatalahu minkum muta'ammidan fa-jaza'un mithlu ma qatala mina al-na'ami yahkumu bihi dhawa 'adlin minkum hadyan baligha al-ka'bati aw kaffaratun ta'amu masakina aw 'adlu dhalika siyaman li-yadhuqa wabala amrihi, 'afa Allahu 'amma salaf, wa-man 'ada fa-yantaqimu Allahu minhu, wa-Allahu 'azizun dhu intiqam

O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. Whoever of you kills it intentionally, the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock, as two men of justice among you judge, as an offering reaching the Kaaba; or an expiation by feeding poor people; or the equivalent of that in fasting, so that he may taste the consequence of his deed. God has pardoned what is past. But whoever returns, God will take retribution from him. And God is Almighty, Lord of retribution.

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.8, p.205, no.247

paragraphs.text: 247 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن أبيه ، عن ابن أبي عمير ، عن حماد بن عثمان قال : تلوت عند أبي عبد الله (﵇) " ذوا عدل منكم (2) " فقال " ذو عدل منكم " هذا مما أخطأت فيه الكتاب .
247. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said.
I recited in the presence of Abu Abd Allah, "two just men from among you."
He said, "'A just man from among you.' This is one of the things the scribes got wrong."

quotes.caption: al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, vol.3, p.416

paragraphs.text: وروي في الشواذ قراءة أبي عبد الرحمن (فجزاء) منون (مثل) منصوب . وقراءة محمد بن علي الباقر ﵇ وجعفر بن محمد الصادق ﵇ : " يحكم به ذو عدل منكم " .

Among the irregular readings, there is reported the reading of Abu Abd al-Rahman, who read “penalty” with tanwin and “equivalent” in the accusative. There is also the reading of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir and Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, “A man of justice among you judges by it.”

quotes.caption: Imam al-Baqir, Tafsir al-Ayyashi, vol.1, p.351, no.200

paragraphs.text: 200 - عن زرارة قال : سمعت أبا جعفر ﵇ يقول : " يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم " قال : ذلك رسول الله ﵌ والامام من بعده ، فإذا حكم به الامام فحسبك
200 - From Zurara, who said,
I heard Abu Jafar say, “Two men of justice among you judge by it.” He said, “That is the Messenger of God and the Imam after him. When the Imam has judged by it, that is enough for you.”

quotes.caption: al-Mazandarani, Sharh Furu' al-Kafi, vol.5, p.199

paragraphs.text: ونسبة الخطأ إليهم لتعميمهم العدلين . هذا هو المشهور في تفسير هذا الكلام ، والأظهر أنّ المراد بالكتّاب نُسّاخ القرآن ، يعني أنّ المنزل كان ذو عدل بلفظ المفرد ، والتثنية من غلطهم .

The attribution of error to them is because they made the “two men of justice” general. This is the well-known view in the interpretation of this statement. The clearer view is that what is meant by the “scribes” is the copyists of the Qur’an. That is, what was revealed was “a man of justice” in the singular form, and the dual form comes from their mistake.

quotes.caption: al-Tabataba'i, Tafsir al-Bayan fi al-Muwafaqa bayn al-Hadith wa al-Qur'an, vol.3, p.336

paragraphs.text: أقول : لفظ الكتّاب بضم الكاف وتشديد التاء المنقوطة ، جمع كاتب يريدان ﵉ كتّاب المصحف
I say, the word al-kuttab, with a damma on the kaf and a doubled dotted ta, is the plural of katib (scribe). The two Imams, al-Baqir and al-Sadiq, mean the scribes of the codex (mushaf).

quotes.caption: al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Wafi, vol.26, p.422

paragraphs.text: بيان : لعل المراد أنه أريد بذي العدل في الآية الإمام المعصوم ، وقد مضى في كتاب الحج .
Explanation. Perhaps what is meant is that the “man of justice” in the verse refers to the infallible Imam. This has already been covered in the Book of Pilgrimage.

quotes.caption: al-Gulpaygani, Taqrirat al-Hajj, vol.3, p.43

paragraphs.text: هذا مما أخطأت به الكتاب (1) . أقول : قوله ﵇ وكذا قول الباقر ﵇ : هذا مما أخطأت به الكتاب المراد من ذلك أن الألف في قوله تعالى " ذوا عدل " زيادة ، قد زاد الكتاب فيه خطأ والصحيح أنه ذو عدل بدون الألف والمراد بذي العدل هو النبي ﵆ أو الإمام الذي بعده . ولكن عن تفسير العياشي عن زرارة قال : سمعت أبا جعفر يقول : " يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم " قال : ذلك رسول الله ﵌ والإمام من بعده ، فإذا حكم به الإمام فحسبك (2) . فيظهر من الرواية أن التثنية في ذوا عدل صحيحة والمراد منهما السول والإمام صلوات الله عليهما وعلى آلهما

“This is one of the things in which the scribes made mistakes.” I say that his statement, and likewise the statement of al-Baqir, “This is one of the things in which the scribes made mistakes,” means that the alif in the words of the Most High, “two men of justice,” is an addition. The scribes added it by mistake, and the correct form is “a man of justice” without the alif. The “man of justice” means the Prophet, or the Imam after him.

But it is reported in the Tafsir of al-Ayyashi, from Zurara, who said, “I heard Abu Jafar say, ‘Two men of justice among you judge by it.’ He said, ‘That is the Messenger of God and the Imam after him. When the Imam has judged by it, that is enough for you.’” It appears from this report that the dual in “two men of justice” is correct, and that what is meant by the two is the Messenger and the Imam, may God’s blessings be upon them both and upon their family.

quotes.caption: Ibn Abbas, al-Mustadrak, vol.2, p.396

paragraphs.text: (حدثنا) أبو علي الحافظ أنبأ عبدان الأهوازي ثنا عمرو بن محمد الناقد ثنا محمد بن يوسف ثنا سفيان عن شعبة عن جعفر بن اياس عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس ﵄ في قوله تعالى لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا قال أخطأ الكاتب حتى تستأذنوا هذا حديث صحيح على شرط الشيخين ولم يخرجاه .

Abu Ali al-Hafiz narrated to us. Abdan al-Ahwazi informed us. Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to us. Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us. Sufyan narrated to us, from Shuba, from Jafar ibn Iyas, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas,
concerning the saying of the Most High, “Do not enter houses other than your own until you become at ease,” he said, “The scribe made a mistake. It is ‘until you ask permission.’”
This hadith is sound by the standard of the two Shaykhs, although they did not record it.

quotes.caption: Ibn Abbas, Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim, vol.8, pp.154-155, no.14560

paragraphs.text: [14560] حدثنا علي بن الحسين ، ثنا نصر بن علي ، أخبرني أبي عن شبل بن عباد عن قيس بن سعد ، عن عطاء عن ابن عباس : (اللَّه نُورُ السَّماواتِ والأَرْضِ مَثَلُ ( نُورِه ) * قال : هي خطأ من الكاتب هو أعظم من أن يكون نوره مثل نور المشكاة قال : مثل نور المؤمن كمشكاة .
[14560] Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us. Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us. My father informed me, from Shibl ibn Abbad, from Qays ibn Sad, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas,

“God is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the likeness of His light.” He said, “It is a mistake by the scribe. He is too great for His light to be like the light of a niche.” He said, “The likeness of the believer’s light is like a niche.”

quotes.caption: Abu Shahba, al-Madkhal, p.365, quoting Abu Hayyan

paragraphs.text: 1 - أن هذا القول غير صحيح في نسبته إلى ابن عباس وهو مدسوس عليه ، دسه الملاحدة والزنادقة ، قال أبو حيان ما نصه : إن من روى عن ابن عباس أنه قال ذلك فهو طاعن في الإسلام ملحد في الدين ، وابن عباس بريء من ذلك القول .

1. This statement is not correctly attributed to Ibn Abbas. It was falsely inserted into his words, and the heretics and the zindiqs inserted it. Abu Hayyan said, in these exact words, "Whoever reports from Ibn Abbas that he said this is attacking Islam and is a heretic in religion, and Ibn Abbas is innocent of that statement."

quotes.caption: Ibn Ashtah, in al-Suyuti, al-Itqan, vol.1, p.557

paragraphs.text: وقد أجاب ابن أشتة عن هذه الآثار كلّها بأنّ المراد أخطئوا في الاختيار ، وما هو الأولى لجمع الناس عليه من الأحرف السبعة ، لا أنّ الذي كتب خطأ خارج عن القرآن .

Ibn Ashtah answered all of these reports by saying that what is meant is that they made a mistake in choosing, from among the seven ahruf, the one that was best for bringing people together. He did not mean that what was written was an error lying outside the Quran.

quotes.caption: Ma'rifat, al-Tamhid fi Ulum al-Qur'an, vol.1, p.370

paragraphs.text: أمّا نفس المحتوى وصحّة ما تضمّنته من تبديل نصّ المصحف الشريف ، فهذا شيء لا نكاد نصدّقه البتة . لأنّه هوالتحريف الذي أجمعت الأُمّة الإسلاميّة على عدم تسرّبه إلى كتاب اللّه العزيز الحميد : «إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ» . (5) فلابدّ من الأخذ في تأويلها إلى وجه معقول أو رفضها رأسا . (6)

As for the content itself, and the soundness of what it contains about altering the text of the noble Mushaf, this is something we can hardly ever believe. It is the very distortion that the Muslim community agreed has never seeped into the Book of God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, "Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians." (Quran 15:9) So one must either interpret these reports in some reasonable way or reject them outright.

quotes.caption: al-Layth, in al-Azhari, Tahdhib al-Lugha, vol.4, p.149

paragraphs.text: قال : وإنما سُمِّي المُصْحَفُ مُصْحَفاً لأنه أُصْحِفَ أي جعل جامعاً للصُّحُف المكتوبة بين الدَّفَّتَيْن .
He said that the mushaf is called a mushaf because it was "ushifa", meaning that it was made a collection of the written sheets between the two covers.

quotes.caption: al-Askari, al-Mushaf fi al-Riwayat wa al-Athar, p.10

paragraphs.text: إنّ المصحف اسم لكلّ كتاب مجلد قرآناً كان أم غير قرآن .
The mushaf is a name for every bound book, whether it is a Quran or not a Quran.

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.239, no.1

paragraphs.text: ثم سكت ساعة ثم قال : وإن عندنا لمصحف فاطمة ﵍ وما يدريهم ما مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ؟ قال : قلت : وما مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ؟ قال : مصحف فيه مثل قرآنكم هذا ثلاث مرات ، والله ما فيه من قرآنكم حرف واحد ، قال : قلت : هذا والله العلم قال : إنه لعلم وما هو بذاك .
Then he was silent for a while, and then he said, "We also have the Mushaf of Fatima. And what do they know of the Mushaf of Fatima?"
He said, "I said, 'And what is the Mushaf of Fatima?'"
He said, "It is a mushaf containing three times the like of this Quran of yours. By God, there is not a single letter of your Quran in it."
He said, "I said, 'This, by God, is knowledge.'"
He said, "It is knowledge, but it is not that."

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.240, no.2

paragraphs.text: 2 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن عمر بن عبد العزيز ، عن حماد بن عثمان قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله ﵇ يقول : تظهر الزنادقة في سنة ثمان وعشرين ومائة وذلك أني نظرت في مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ، قال : قلت : وما مصحف فاطمة ؟ قال : إن الله تعالى لما قبض نبيه ﵌ دخل على فاطمة ﵍ من وفاته من الحزن ما لا يعلمه إلا الله ﷿ فأرسل الله إليها ملكا يسلي غمها ويحدثها ، فشكت ذلك (1) إلى أمير المؤمنين ﵇ فقال : إذا أحسست بذلك وسمعت الصوت قولي لي فأعلمته بذلك فجعل أمير المؤمنين ﵇ يكتب كلما سمع حتى أثبت من ذلك مصحفا قال : ثم قال : أما إنه ليس فيه شئ من الحلال والحرام ولكن فيه علم ما يكون .
2. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said that he heard Abu Abd Allah say,
"The heretics will appear in the year one hundred and twenty-eight, and that is because I looked in the Mushaf of Fatima."
He said, "I said, 'And what is the Mushaf of Fatima?'"

He said, "When God the Exalted took back His Prophet, there came upon Fatima, because of his death, a grief that only God the Mighty and Majestic knows. So God sent her an angel to console her in her sorrow and to speak with her. She complained of this to the Commander of the Believers, and he said, 'When you sense that and hear the voice, tell me.' She told him about it, and the Commander of the Believers began to write down everything he heard, until he had put together a mushaf from it."
He said, "Then he said, 'It contains nothing of the lawful and the unlawful, but it contains knowledge of what will happen.'"

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.240, no.3

paragraphs.text: 3 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، عن الحسين ابن أبي العلاء قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله ﵇ يقول : إن عندي الجفر الأبيض ، قال : قلت : فأي شئ فيه ؟ قال : زبور داود ، وتوراة موسى ، وإنجيل عيسى ، وصحف إبراهيم ﵈ والحلال والحرام ، ومصحف فاطمة ، ما أزعم أن فيه قرآنا ، وفيه ما يحتاج الناس إلينا ولا نحتاج إلى أحد حتى فيه الجلدة ، ونصف الجلدة ، وربع الجلدة وأرش الخدش .
3. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala, who said that he heard Abu Abd Allah say,
"I have the White Jafr."
He said, "I said, 'And what is in it?'"

He said, "The Psalms of David, the Torah of Moses, the Gospel of Jesus, the scrolls of Abraham, the lawful and the unlawful, and the Mushaf of Fatima. I do not claim that it contains a Quran. It contains what people need from us, while we need nothing from anyone. It even contains the lash, the half lash, the quarter lash, and the compensation for a scratch."

quotes.caption: Imam Ali, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.64, no.1

paragraphs.text: فما نزلت على رسول الله ﵌ آية من القرآن إلا أقرأنيها وأملاها علي فكتبتها بخطي وعلمني تأويلها وتفسيرها وناسخها ومنسوخها ، ومحكمها ومتشابهها ، وخاصها وعامها ، ودعا الله أن يعطيني فهمها ، وحفظها ، فما نسيت آية من كتاب الله ولا علما أملاه علي وكتبته ، منذ دعا الله لي بما دعا ، وما ترك شيئا علمه الله من حلال ولا حرام ، ولا أمر ولا نهي كان أو يكون ولا كتاب منزل على أحد قبله من طاعة أو معصية إلا علمنيه وحفظته ، فلم أنس حرفا واحدا

No verse of the Quran was sent down to the Messenger of God except that he had me recite it and dictated it to me, and I wrote it in my own hand. He taught me its interpretation (ta'wil) and its explanation (tafsir), its abrogating and abrogated verses, its decisive and ambiguous verses, and its particular and general verses.

He prayed to God to give me understanding of it and memory of it. So I have not forgotten a verse of the Book of God, nor any knowledge that he dictated to me and I wrote down, since he prayed to God for me as he prayed.

He left nothing that God had taught him, whether permitted or forbidden, command or prohibition, what has been or what will be, or any book sent down to anyone before him, whether of obedience or of disobedience, except that he taught it to me and I memorized it. I did not forget a single letter.

quotes.caption: Imam Ali, al-Ihtijaj, vol.1, p.281

paragraphs.text: فلما توفي رسول الله ﵌ اشتغلت بدفنه والفراغ من شأنه ثم آليت يمينا (1) أني لا أرتدي إلا للصلاة حتى أجمع القرآن ففعلت ، ثم أخذته وجئت به فأعرضته عليهم قالوا : لا حاجة لنا به

When the Messenger of God died, I was occupied with burying him and finishing his affairs. Then I swore an oath that I would not put on my cloak except for prayer until I had collected the Quran, and I did so. Then I took it, brought it, and presented it to them.
They said, "We have no need of it."

quotes.caption: Imam Ali, Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 176, p.252

paragraphs.text: واعْلَمُوا أَنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ هُوَ النَّاصِحُ الَّذِي لَا يَغُشُّ - والْهَادِي الَّذِي لَا يُضِلُّ والْمُحَدِّثُ الَّذِي لَا يَكْذِبُ
Know that this Quran is the adviser who does not deceive, the guide who does not lead astray, and the speaker who does not lie.

quotes.caption: Imam Ali, Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 156, p.219

paragraphs.text: وعَلَيْكُمْ بِكِتَابِ اللَّه - فَإِنَّه الْحَبْلُ الْمَتِينُ والنُّورُ الْمُبِينُ - والشِّفَاءُ النَّافِعُ والرِّيُّ النَّاقِعُ - والْعِصْمَةُ لِلْمُتَمَسِّكِ والنَّجَاةُ لِلْمُتَعَلِّقِ - لَا يَعْوَجُّ فَيُقَامَ ولَا يَزِيغُ فَيُسْتَعْتَبَ - ولَا تُخْلِقُه كَثْرَةُ الرَّدِّ ووُلُوجُ السَّمْعِ - مَنْ قَالَ بِه صَدَقَ ومَنْ عَمِلَ بِه سَبَقَ

Hold fast to the Book of God, for it is the firm rope and the clear light, the beneficial cure and the quenching drink, a protection for whoever holds to it and a rescue for whoever clings to it. It does not bend, so that it would need straightening, and it does not swerve, so that it would need to be turned back. Repeated recitation and constant hearing do not wear it out. Whoever speaks by it speaks truly, and whoever acts by it takes the lead.

quotes.caption: al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208

paragraphs.text: وروى جماعة ، عن عمرو بن الصباح ، عن حفص الغاضري ، عن عاصم ، عن أبي عبد الرحمن ، عن علي بالقراءة . وذكر عاصم أنه لم يخالف أبا عبد الرحمن في شيء من قراءته ، وأن أبا عبد الرحمن لم يخالف عليا في شيء من قراءته .
A group transmitted from Amr ibn al-Sabbah, from Hafs al-Ghadiri, from Asim, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, concerning the recitation.
Asim mentioned that he never differed from Abu Abd al-Rahman in any part of his recitation, and that Abu Abd al-Rahman never differed from Ali in any part of his recitation.

quotes.caption: Hafs, in al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208

paragraphs.text: ويروى عن حفص بن سليمان ، قال : قال لي عاصم : ما كان من القراءة التي قرأت بها على أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي ، فهي التي أقرأتك بها ، وما كان من القراءة التي أقرأت بها أبا بكر بن عياش ، فهي القراءة التي عرضتها على زرّ بن حبيش ، عن ابن مسعود .
It is reported from Hafs ibn Sulayman, who said.

Asim said to me, “Whatever recitation I recited to Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, that is the one I taught you. And whatever recitation I taught Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, that is the recitation I presented to Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Masud.”

quotes.caption: the introduction to the Cairo printing, in al-Tabrizi, Tanzih al-Shi'a al-Ithnay Ashariyya, vol.1, p.41

paragraphs.text: تعريف بهذا المصحف الشريف كتب هذا المصحف وضبط على ما يوافق رواية حفص بن سليمان بن المغيرة الأسدي الكوفي بقراءة عاصم بن أبي النجود الكوفي التابعي ، عن أبي عبد الرحمن عبد الله بن حبيب السلمي ، عن عثمان بن عفان ، وعلي بن أبي طالب ﵇ ، وزيد بن ثابت ، وأبي بن كعب ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه (وآله) وسلم .

Introduction to this noble Quran codex. This codex was written and vocalized in agreement with the transmission of Hafs ibn Sulayman ibn al-Mughira al-Asadi al-Kufi, from the recitation of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Kufi, a Follower, from Abu Abd al-Rahman Abd Allah ibn Habib al-Sulami, from Uthman ibn Affan, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Zayd ibn Thabit and Ubayy ibn Kab, from the Prophet.

quotes.caption: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, in Ibn Mihran, al-Mabsut, p.440

paragraphs.text: واختار أبو بكر بن عياش {عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ} خفيفة الراء أيضا . وهو من الحروف العشرة التي ذكرت أنه قال : " أنا أدخلتها من قراءة علي - ﵁ - في قراءة عاصم حتى استخلصت قراءته " . يعني قراءة علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ .

Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash also chose the reading "he acknowledged part of it" with a light ra. It is one of the ten readings concerning which I mentioned that he said, "I introduced them from the reading of Ali into the reading of Asim, until I had distilled his reading." He means the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib.

quotes.caption: al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, vol.2, p.183

paragraphs.text: قرأ حمزة والكسائي " فارقوا دينهم " وهي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب : أي تركوا دينهم وخرجوا عنه . وقرأ الباقون فرقوا بالتشديد إلا النخعي فإنه قرأ بالتخفيف .
